title: Fabrication of Ti3C2 MXene Microelectrode Arrays for In Vivo Neural Recording
protocol: Prepare the selective etching solution in a 125 mL plastic container by adding 12 mL of deionized water (DI H2O) followed by 24 mL of hydrochloric acid (HCl).
Add 4 mL of HF to the etchant container.
Slowly add 2 g of Ti3AlC2 MAX phase to the reaction container and stir with a Teflon magnetic bar for 24 h at 35 °C at 400 rpm.
Fill two 175 mL centrifuge tubes with 100 mL of DI H2O.
Split the etching reaction mixture into 175 mL centrifuge tubes and wash the material by repeated centrifugation at 3,500 rpm for 5 min.
Decant the acidic supernatant into a plastic hazardous waste container.
Repeat washing until the pH reaches 6.
Add 2 g of lithium chloride (LiCl) to 100 mL of DI H2O and stir at 200 rpm until dissolved.
Mix 100 mL of LiCl/H2O with the Ti3C2/Ti3AlC2 sediment and stir the reaction for 12 h at 25 °C.
Wash the intercalation reaction in 175 mL centrifuge tubes by centrifuging at 2,550 x g for 5 min.
Decant the clear supernatant.
Repeat washing until a dark supernatant is found.
Continue to centrifuge for 1 h at 2,550 x g.
Decant the dilute-green supernatant.
Re-disperse the swollen sediment with 150 mL of DI H2O.
Transfer supernatant to 50 mL centrifuge tubes and centrifuge at 2,550 x g for 10 min.
Separate remaining MAX (sediment) from MXene (supernatant).
Collect supernatant as Ti3C2 MXene.
Perform further size selection by collecting the supernatant following a centrifugation step at 2,550 x g for 1 h.
Argon bubble the solutions for 30 min prior to packaging in an Argon sealed headspace vial (transfer via a syringe).
Store solutions at high concentrations (>5 mg/mL), away from sunlight, and at low temperatures (≤5 °C) to ensure longevity.
Deposit a 4 μm thick bottom layer of parylene-C onto a clean Si wafer.
Use the first photomask (mask-1) to define the metal interconnects of the devices, as well as a metal ring around the edge of the wafer to aid in later lift-off steps.
Spin coat NR71-3000p onto the wafer at 3,000 rpm for 40 s.
Soft bake the wafer on a hot plate for 14.5 min at 95 °C.
Load the wafer and mask-1 into a mask aligner.
Position the wafer so that the ring on the photomask overlaps with all edges of the wafer.
Expose with i-line at a dose of 90 mJ/cm².
Hard bake the wafer on a hot plate for 1 min at 115 °C.
Immerse the wafer in the RD6 developer for 2 min, continuously agitating the solution.
Rinse the wafer thoroughly with DI H₂O.
Blow dry the wafer with an N₂ gun.
Deposit 10 nm Ti using an electron beam evaporator at a base pressure of 5 x 10⁻⁷ Torr and a rate of 2 Å/s.
Deposit 100 nm Au onto the wafer using the same conditions as for Ti.
Immerse the wafer in remover PG for ~10 min until the photoresist has dissolved.
Sonicate the wafer for 30 s to remove any remaining traces of unwanted metal.
Rinse the wafer first in clean remover PG solution, then thoroughly rinse in DI H₂O.
Dry the wafer with an N₂ gun.
Expose the wafer to O₂ plasma for 30 s.
Spin coat a 2% cleaning solution (e.g., Micro-90) in DI H₂O onto the wafer at 1,000 rpm for 30 s.
Allow the wafer to air dry for at least 5 min.
Deposit 3 μm of parylene-C onto the wafer.
Repeat steps for mask-2 and align the alignment marks between wafer and photomask before exposure.
Use O2 plasma reactive ion etching (RIE) to etch through the sacrificial parylene-C layer in areas not covered by photoresist.
Confirm complete etching of sacrificial parylene-C layer using profilometer.
Spin-coat MXene solution onto wafer.
Pipette MXene solution onto each desired pattern, then spin wafer at 1000 rpm for 40 s.
Dry the wafer on a 120 °C hot plate for 10 min to remove residual water from MXene film.
Use electron beam evaporator to deposit 50 nm SiO2 onto wafer as protective layer.
Remove the sacrificial parylene-C layer to pattern the MXene and SiO2 layers.
Apply a small drop of DI H2O to the edge of the wafer using tweezers to peel up the sacrificial parylene-C layer, beginning where its edges are defined in the ring around the outside of the wafer.
Rinse the wafer thoroughly in DI H2O to remove any remaining cleaning solution residue.
Dry the wafer with an N2 gun.
Place the wafer on a 120 °C hot plate for 1 h to remove any residual water from the patterned MXene films.
Deposit a 4 μm thick top layer of parylene-C.
Use the third photomask (mask-3) to define device outline and openings over electrodes and Au bonding pads (VIAs).
Repeat steps involving mask alignment, exposure, and metal deposition using mask-3.
Carefully align the alignment marks between the wafer and photomask before exposure.
Deposit 100 nm Al onto the wafer using an electron beam evaporator.
Immerse the wafer in remover PG for ~10 min until the metal has fully lifted off, leaving Al covering the devices with openings for electrodes and bonding pads.
Sonicate the wafer for 30 s to remove any remaining traces of unwanted metal.
Rinse the wafer first in clean remover PG solution.
Thoroughly rinse the wafer in DI H2O.
Dry the wafer with an N2 gun.
Etch the parylene-C to pattern the device outline and openings over electrodes and Au bonding pads.
Use O2 plasma RIE to etch through the parylene-C layers surrounding the devices.
Etch through the top parylene-C layer covering both the MXene electrode contacts and the Au bonding pads.
Etch the Al layer using a wet chemical etch in Al etchant type A at 50 °C for 10 min or until all visual traces of Al have disappeared, whichever comes first.
Etch the SiO2 covering the MXene electrodes using a wet chemical etch in 6:1 buffered oxide etchant (BOE) for 30 s.
Place a small drop of DI H2O at the edge of a device to release it from the Si substrate wafer.
Gently peel up the device as water is wicked underneath it by capillary action.
Interface thin film microelectrode arrays with an adapter for connection to the electrophysiology recording system.

Use a printed circuit board (PCB) with a zero-insertion force (ZIF) connector for interfacing with the Au bonding pads on the microelectrode array and another connector for interfacing with the head-stage of the recording system.
Apply a thin film of solder paste to each contact pad on the PCB.
Place Omnetics and ZIF connectors in their appropriate locations on the PCB.
Heat the assembly on a hot plate until the solder reflows, forming connections.
Apply two layers of polyimide tape to the back side of the Au bonding pad region of the MXene microelectrode array.
Trim any excess tape beyond the edges of the parylene-C device using a razor blade or precision scissors.
Align the MXene microelectrode array in the ZIF connector so that the Au bonding pads align with the pins inside the ZIF connector.
Close the ZIF to form a secure connection.
Test the electrochemical impedance of the MXene electrodes using a potentiostat.
Perform surgeries on adult male Sprague Dawley rats using sterile instruments and aseptic technique.
Check respiratory rate, palpebral reflex, and pedal pinch reflex every 10 min during surgery to monitor depth of anesthesia.
Maintain body temperature with a heating pad during the procedure.
Administer preemptive analgesia via subcutaneous injection of buprenorphine sustained release (SR) at 1.2 mg/kg.
Inject anesthesia intraperitoneally using a mixture of 60 mg/kg ketamine and 0.25 mg/kg dexmedetomidine.
Confirm proper level of anesthesia every 10 min throughout the experiment by checking for absence of palpebral and pedal pinch reflexes.
Secure the rat in a stereotaxic frame and apply ocular lubricant to the eyes.
Clean the shaved scalp with 10% povidone-iodine.
Expose the calvaria with a single midline scalp incision and blunt dissection of underlying tissue.
Place a 00-90 screw into the skull for grounding recordings.
Use a dental drill with a small burr to make a craniotomy at the desired cortical recording site.
Secure the array connector to a stereotaxic manipulator and position it over the craniotomy.
Gently lower the device until the entire array is in contact with the exposed cortex.
Wrap the ground wire around the skull screw.
Connect the recording system headstage to the array and begin recording spontaneous activity.
